issue.title: An unreadable plugins.json is carried in a backup or sync as no plugins
issue.body:
Found while fixing #2269 (707fbb249). `backup.Collect` carries the plugin list through `provider.Carried` -> `plugin.Load` -> `plugin.list` (internal/plugin/store.go), which returns an empty `List{}` when plugins.json is there but can't be read (and has no good `.bak`). So a backup or a sync made then carries "no plugins".

What it does today: on another computer `bring` adds plugins and never removes one, so nothing is uninstalled elsewhere. But the server's bundle loses the list until this computer reads the file again, so a computer that joins in between gets no plugins, and an exported backup has none.

Fix direction: give the carry path a checked read (an error for "there but unreadable"), and have `Collect` stop on it as it does for providers.json and settings.json. Not changed in 707fbb249 to keep that commit to the destructive case.

comments.body:
Patch for this, one commit on current `main` (d0ccbbeb):

- Compare: https://github.com/yetone/magpie/compare/main...ump45nose:magpie:fix/2287-backup-unreadable-plugins
- Patch for `git am`: https://github.com/ump45nose/magpie/commit/e930262825451d8a1e0df08f8ae8623eddc0c110.patch

**Root cause.** `backup.Collect` → `provider.Carried` → `plugin.Load` → `plugin.list` gets an empty `List{}` when `lastgood.Read` fails. That covers plugins.json being there but unreadable with no good `.bak`, so a backup, an export or a sync carried "no plugins".

**Fix.** I added `plugin.LoadChecked` (via `listChecked`), which returns that error. A missing file is still no plugins with no error. `provider.Carried` now returns `([]plugin.Entry, error)`, and `Collect` stops on the error the same way it does for providers.json and settings.json (#2269): nothing gets sealed or pushed, and the sync status shows the error. `plugin.Load` behaves the same as before for its other callers. I also updated `docs/subsystems/sync-backup.md`.

**Failing without the fix** (new tests, old code):
```
--- FAIL: TestCollectStopsOnUnreadablePlugins
    plugins_unreadable_test.go:34: Collect read a plugins.json that can't be read as no plugins: <nil> []
--- FAIL: TestSyncStopsOnUnreadablePlugins
    unreadable_test.go:208: a synced a broken plugins.json
```
With the fix, both pass, and so do `TestPluginsCarried` and `TestRestorePluginsAndSignIn`.

**Checks run** (Linux x86_64, temp HOME with Go caches pinned): `gofmt -l` is clean. `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...`, `GOOS=windows go vet ./...` and `GOOS=darwin go vet -tags nogui ./...` are clean, and so are the matching three `go build`s. In `go test -tags nogui ./...` every package passes except internal/agent (6 tests), internal/plugin (4 bun/proxy tests) and internal/gateway (`TestPluginModelListThroughAccountProxy`). Those same tests fail the same way on unmodified `d0ccbbeb` in this sandbox.
**Not run:** darwin vet/build without `nogui` (needs cgo and the macOS SDK), a real WebDAV/S3/GitHub server, and Windows.

AI assistance disclosure: an AI coding assistant wrote this patch and comment, and I reviewed them.

Published a fix in my fork: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/commit/c43ab301138e62548f72602a3dfd5a8f13fb83db

Thanks for the report and @ump45nose for the patch. I adapted e930262825451d8a1e0df08f8ae8623eddc0c110 onto the cumulative fork branch, preserving Co-authored-by attribution.

The shared plugin-list reader now exposes its read error through plugin.LoadChecked, provider.Carried and backup.Collect. A backup/export or setup sync stops when plugins.json is unreadable instead of carrying “no plugins”. Missing files still mean no plugins; a valid last-good .bak still supplies the list. Existing unchecked plugin readers keep their behavior, Load still returns a mutable copy, and carry filtering for local paths/secrets remains covered. The sync/backup reference is updated.

Verification: TestCollectStopsOnUnreadablePlugins and TestSyncStopsOnUnreadablePlugins both fail with the old product code (nil error/empty list; sync accepts the broken file). With the fix, they pass alongside TestPluginsCarried and TestRestorePluginsAndSignIn under -race -count=5. The backup regression also checks valid .bak recovery and a missing file. The sync regression checks no PUT, the original broken file left intact, the error in status, and the original plugin list retained on the fake WebDAV server.

At this exact commit all seven acceptance commands passed with Go1.26.8, temporary HOME and pinned caches: native Linux vet/build, Linux nogui vet/build, Windows vet/build, and go test -tags nogui ./... -count=1 -timeout=45m (69 packages). Gofmt and whitespace checks are clean.

Combined branch: https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/issue-batch-20261023-x

Not checked: a live WebDAV/S3/GitHub sync service, a Windows file held open by another process, or Windows/macOS runtime. The regression uses a truncated plugins.json and an HTTP fixture. No live gateway/config changed and no upstream PR opened.

issue.title: backup, davsync: a settings.json that can't be read is carried into a backup and a sync as the defaults, taking the settings of every other machine it is put back on

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
**What's wrong**

`backup.Collect` asked `os.Stat` whether `settings.json` was there and then took the settings from `settings.Load` (`internal/backup/backup.go:211` on main at 9916a946). `Load` stands its defaults in for a file that is there but can't be read, or doesn't parse and has no good `.bak` — the case `settings.LoadChecked` exists for, and the case `provider.Stored` refuses for `providers.json` (9c54a560: "a providers.json that can't be read is said where the providers are listed, never backed up or synced as none"). So an unreadable `settings.json` travelled as the user's own settings: theme `system`, language `system`, text size 110, an empty `AllowIPs`, no disabled models, and none of the per-model names, prices, efforts, wires or output caps.

That bundle is then this computer's settings part: `davsync.collect` (`internal/davsync/davsync.go:762`) seals and pushes it, and the part's hash differing from the last sync reads as "changed here" (`davsync.go:1164`, `lc && !rc` → `take`), so the defaults go up as if the user had changed their settings. Every other computer brings a server-changed part in (`bring` → `backup.Restore`, `davsync.go:962`), and Restore ends in `settings.Save` (`internal/backup/backup.go:456`), which refuses only when that machine's own file can't be read. The other machine's file reads fine; its theme, language, text size, allow list and per-model settings are written over. `KeepOwn` puts back only the window, proxy, port, tray and consent that are this computer's own, so nothing stands in the way, and nothing is said — the status shows a normal sync. The same holds for a backup file exported while the file is unreadable (`magpie backup`, the GUI's export): it carries the defaults, and importing it anywhere erases those settings there.

Triggers, all without a gesture from the user: a Windows handle another program holds for a moment (an editor, a backup tool, antivirus), a permission magpie doesn't have, a file another tool wrote that isn't JSON, and the zeroed or cut-short file class #1505 exists for.

**Why this is exceptionally important**

- **Who pays**: every other machine on the sync — one unreadable read on one computer rewrites the settings of all the others, silently, and each following sync keeps them. Also anyone restoring a backup made while the file was unreadable.
- **What is lost**: the preferences that are the point of the settings file — theme, language, text size, the gateway's `AllowIPs`, disabled models, and every per-model name, price, reasoning effort, wire and output cap.
- **The project's own rule**: "a failed read, parse or hash means unknown" (LESSONS.md; moved into docs/code-standards.md on 10-13). It was applied to this same file on 10-12 (7d9382db2: an unreadable settings.json let every address into the gateway) and to providers (9c54a560). `backup.Collect` kept the old read for settings, and it is the carry node for the backup, the sync and the GUI export, so this is the remaining path of the same defect class.
- **Scale**: sync is a shipped feature (WebDAV, S3, GitHub) that runs every three minutes once configured; the repo has 12,661 stars / 863 forks and the current release's assets take ~1,000 downloads in their first hours (the same figures as #2242). A user with two computers and one damaged file loses the settings on both — the pushed defaults come back around with the next sync.
- **It stays until fixed**: no release changes the read, and the damaged machine re-pushes the defaults on its next sync.

**Minimal reproduction** (main at 9916a946)

Two tests from the fix's branch, both real `FAIL`s on main. `TestCollectStopsOnUnreadableSettings` (internal/backup; a home whose `settings.json` is cut short, no `.bak`):

`TestSyncStopsOnUnreadableSettings` (internal/davsync; two computers join over a fake WebDAV, a's file is cut short):

```
--- FAIL: TestSyncStopsOnUnreadableSettings (9.71s)
    unreadable_test.go:131: a synced a broken settings.json
FAIL

```

With the branch's fix both pass:

```
ok  	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/backup	0.955s
ok  	github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/davsync	10.854s
```

With the guard written as if it were there but never taken (`err != nil && err == nil`), both fail again with the same lines.

**The fix, since this account cannot open a pull request on this repo** (the README: "This repository doesn't take pull requests. Only maintainers can open them."; the API refuses: "JasonBuildAI does not have the correct permissions to execute CreatePullRequest", REST 404 — the same as #2229, #2231, #2239 and #2242): branch `fix/599409-tbd` in the fork `JasonBuildAI/magpie`, commit `2ac0bb2d` on main at 9916a946:

```
git fetch https://github.com/JasonBuildAI/magpie fix/599409-tbd && git cherry-pick FETCH_HEAD
```

- `internal/backup/backup.go`: `Collect` reads through `settings.LoadChecked` and stops the backup with the file's error, exactly as it stops on a `providers.json` that can't be read; only a file that is there and reads is carried.
- `internal/backup/settings_unreadable_test.go`: `TestCollectStopsOnUnreadableSettings`.
- `internal/davsync/unreadable_test.go`: `TestSyncStopsOnUnreadableSettings`, the settings sibling of `TestSyncStopsOnUnreadableProviders`: two computers join, a's file is cut short, a's sync ends in the error with nothing pushed and the file left alone, the server still carries a's real settings, and b, syncing after, keeps them.

Semantic change: for a `settings.json` that is there but can't be read or parsed with no last-good `.bak`, a backup, a sync and an export now stop with that file's error, where they previously carried the defaults and let them travel to the other machines; a missing file, an empty one, and one with a good `.bak` (read as the last good generation) are unchanged. No interface, state or compatibility change; `davsync` needs no change of its own, the error propagates from `Collect` through `collect` before anything is sealed or pushed.

Ran on the branch: `gofmt -l` on the three files prints nothing; `go vet ./internal/backup ./internal/davsync` exit 0; `GOOS=linux go vet -tags nogui ./...` exit 0; `GOOS=windows go vet ./...` exit 0; `GOOS=linux go build -tags nogui ./...` exit 0; `GOOS=windows go build ./...` exit 0; the two `-run` tests above pass (`ok 0.955s` and `ok 10.854s`). `go test -tags nogui -count=1 ./...` is running as this is posted — this box is running several agents' suites at once at 91% CPU — and its result will follow in a comment. Not tried: a live WebDAV or S3 server, and a Windows file held open; the reproduction is the cut-short file, which is the same "there but unreadable" the read sees.

AI disclosure: this change was drafted with AI assistance at my request, under my direction and review.
